channel.title: Morning Brief — Australia Edition
channel.description: A short daily news brief covering Australian national news, Queensland, and the Gold Coast — made to listen to on the morning drive.
channel.itunes:author: Rogineh

item.title: Morning Brief — Friday, 25 September 2026
item.description: Today: a former NGV employee is charged over an alleged $8 million phone theft scheme; Brisbane Showgrounds early works begin within weeks as part of 2032 Olympic legacy infrastructure; and the Gold Coast's BLEACH Festival returns with its biggest ever program, moving to a spring October date. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (오늘의 브리핑 영어 방송 후 한국어 전체 브리핑이 이어집니다).

item.title: Morning Brief — Thursday, 24 September 2026
item.description: Today: the federal Thriving Kids program launches October 1 with every state signed on except Queensland, sparking a Canberra-Brisbane standoff over funding and eligibility detail; and Gold Coast hinterland residents brace for smoke haze as hazard reduction burns continue around Mount Nathan, Clagiraba, Wongawallan, and Tamborine. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (오늘의 브리핑 영어 방송 후 한국어 전체 브리핑이 이어집니다).

item.title: Morning Brief — Wednesday, 23 September 2026
item.description: Today: the big four banks now forecast an RBA rate rise next week as Canberra schools brace for a delayed Thursday start; Brisbane sets up a blockbuster NRLW preliminary final against Gold Coast; and Cbus Super Stadium in Robina gears up to host Sunday's showdown. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (오늘의 브리핑 영어 방송 후 한국어 전체 브리핑이 이어집니다).

item.title: Morning Brief — Tuesday, 22 September 2026
item.description: Today: Australia posts 1.2 million new jobs over four years with unemployment at a 50-year low; Queensland Rail and seven unions settle a nine-month pay dispute with full services returning by November; and the Gold Coast confirms a $226 million investment in sport and community facilities. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (오늘의 브리핑 영어 방송 후 한국어 전체 브리핑이 이어집니다).

item.description: Today: fuel prices climb again as Middle East disruption hits oil markets and Adelaide edges Brisbane in a fiery AFLW clash; Queensland police search for a missing Greenvale man as regional tourism and agriculture operators raise migration concerns; and the Gold Coast Suns rout Essendon while the city gears up for a busy spring events calendar. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (오늘의 브리핑 영어 방송 후 한국어 전체 브리핑이 이어집니다).

item.description: Today: a US-funded search off Broome wraps up as the Junior Matildas qualify for the U-17 World Cup; Brisbane and Moreton detectives charge two men over 81 property offences and a Southport teen faces a Wavell Heights burglary charge; and HOTA welcomes the White Rabbit Collection and a new Children's Gallery exhibition to the Gold Coast. item.description: Today: Europe reacts to Australia skipping West Bank trade sanctions as SunRice job cuts hit a small Riverina town hard; the QAFL Grand Final caps off the season and a woman is charged over an alleged cash for demerit points scheme; and the Gold Coast Suns call in the Titans to fix their tackling ahead of an AFLW trade shake-up. item.description: Today: Australia and New Zealand are floated as potential EU associate members as population growth hits 1.4%; a Queensland driving crackdown nets 81 charges and Far North Queensland beekeepers lose hives worth $20,000; and the Gold Coast unveils a 20-year vision for 185,000 new homes ahead of a Pink Ribbon Raceday. item.description: Today: oil prices spike on a Saudi supply disruption and a century-old murder hotel hits the market in WA; a Brisbane BMX rider's Scientology speedrun stunt lands him in court alongside a serious pedestrian assault case; and a revamped Gold Coast bus network rolls out as part of a $543m transport investment. item.description: Today: new research finds Australia's pre-colonial Indigenous population was far larger than previously thought, and global bond yields climb past 5%; a Mount Isa suburb is overwhelmed by flying foxes and Brisbane detectives charge a man with 42 property offences; and the Gold Coast takes a housing affordability ruling to the High Court as police charge 15 people in a major drug operation. item.description: Today: political leaders condemn Pauline Hanson's resurfaced Indigenous comments and the Sydney Roosters cap a record NRLW season; a destructive bee mite reaches its northernmost detection in Far North Queensland and a coronial inquest hears from a missing woman's daughter; and a Gold Coast gang-recruitment crackdown nets fifteen charges as the city trials a pedestrian-only Surfers Paradise esplanade. item.title: Morning Brief — Monday, 14 September 2026
item.description: Today: proposed online-harm powers face pushback, mortgage rate competition heats up, and pensioners face health rebate cuts; Queensland investigates a residential-care assault case and coalmine security; and the Gold Coast deals with weekend traffic chaos and a hazard-reduction burn. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (호주, 퀵즐랜드, 그리고 골드코스트 소식을 전해드립니다).

item.title: Morning Brief — Sunday, 13 September 2026
item.description: Today: a looming lift on the plug-in solar ban, South Australia's aged-care bed-block costs, Queensland's weekend bushfire outbreak and a $1 million cold-case reward, and a Coomera townhouse fire on the Gold Coast. Broadcast in English, followed by a full Korean-language version (호주, 퀵즐랜드, 그리고 골드코스트 소식을 전해드립니다. 영어 방송 후 한국어 전체 브리핑이 이어집니다).
